content: 1. The absorption of oral digoxin may be reduced if it is taken with meals that are high in bran fiber. 2. It is currently unknown whether alcohol consumption affects the efficacy or safety of digoxin. 3. Drinking alcohol while taking digoxin may increase the risk of side effects such as dizziness, blurred vision, and confusion. 4. Digoxin has the potential to interact with many other medications. 5. In the event of a digoxin overdose, immediately stop taking the medication and seek medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. 6. If you miss a dose of digoxin, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. 7. Individuals who are allergic to digoxin, digitalis, Lanoxin, or any ingredients in the specific product should not take digoxin. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients. 8. Digoxin should not be used in patients with a type of abnormal heart rhythm called ventricular fibrillation. 9. Only take digoxin if it has been prescribed to you by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and do not share the medication with others, even if they have the same condition. 10. Keep digoxin out of the reach of children. 11. Digoxin may impair alertness or coordination. Avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you know how the medication affects you. 12. Digoxin can influence blood pressure and heart rate. Discuss with your healthcare provider how to monitor these symptoms. 13. If prescribed digoxin oral solution, use the oral syringe provided in the package to measure your dose accurately. Consult your pharmacist if you are unsure how to measure the dose. 14. Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using. This helps determine if digoxin is appropriate for you. 15. Specifically, inform your healthcare provider if you have conditions such as Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, sinus node disease, AV block, kidney problems, myocarditis, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, thyroid issues, chronic diarrhea, or a history of electrolyte imbalances (e.g., low potassium, magnesium, or calcium levels, or high calcium levels). 16. Notify your healthcare provider if you are undergoing a medical procedure like electrical cardioversion, as digoxin may interact with the procedure. 17. Digoxin passes into breast milk. Inform your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed. 18. The effects of digoxin on pregnancy and an unborn baby are not well understood. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. They will advise you on whether to continue or avoid digoxin during pregnancy. 19. Digoxin may interact with other medications and supplements. Inform your healthcare provider about all substances you are taking to avoid potential interactions. 20.
